page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 belongs to the general-purpose N1 machine family, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The virtualization layer provides simultaneous multithreading with two threads per physical core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 120 GB, establishing a standard memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage requirements.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a clear separation between single-threaded execution speed and aggregate multi-core throughput. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (score of 922.0) and stress-ng place the processor in lower baseline percentiles, reflecting the modest 2.3 GHz clock frequency and older instruction set support, which lacks AVX-512 extensions. Conversely, multi-threaded performance stabilizes within median ranges, as evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 7982.0, a PassMark CPU score of 20859.21, and steady multi-threaded compression metrics. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 101.81 GB/sec with write speeds at 46.41 GB/sec, ensuring stable data flow under concurrent execution.

Resource distribution makes n1-standard-32 a practical solution for workloads that demand steady aggregate concurrency rather than high per-core execution speeds. The system registers 21.91 million Redis SET operations per second and handles static web serving throughput at 18.23 GB/sec, reflecting capability in network and memory-bound environments. Small and medium language model prompt processing operates at average throughput, though larger parameter models reveal execution constraints. The instance offers reliable multi-core resource density for distributed enterprise software, batch ETL pipelines, medium-scale databases, and web serving clusters.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel Xeon cores at a 2.3 GHz base frequency. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled, the instance includes 45 MB of L3 cache and provides 120 GB of system memory, matching a standard 3.75 GB per core allocation. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread execution, placing single-core performance metrics in lower percentiles, while parallel capacity reaches average industry thresholds across multi-core tests, database operations, and memory bandwidth. The system handles memory-intensive multithreaded loads efficiently, achieving 21.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.23 GB/s static web serving throughput. n1-standard-32 is primarily aligned with scale-out application tiers, multi-threaded batch jobs, caching layers, and enterprise web services that prioritize aggregate throughput over individual core speed.
